sentences.text:
By order dated 23.02.2023, he has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life, to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further suffer R.I. for six months under Section 364 of the IPC; imprisonment for life, to pay a fine of Rs.
25,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further suffer R.I. for one year under Section 302 of the IPC; imprisonment for three years, to pay a fine of Rs. 3,000/- and in default of payment of fine,
to further suffer S.I. for two months under Section 201 of the IPC; and imprisonment for life, to pay a fine of Rs. 25,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to further suffer R.I. for one year under Pradeep Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95342182/
1 Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
3. The sentences have been ordered to run concurrently.
4. The appellant is a relative of the deceased and was staying in the house of the deceased at the Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: APP (DB) No.503 of 2023(4) dt.07-10-2024 time of the occurrence.

The mother of the deceased had lodged the FIR that some untoward overtures were made by the appellant towards the victim, a five and a half years old girl; but on being chastised by the mother of the victim, the appellant went away.
Later, the victim was not to be found in the house.
The appellant had his clothes and hand and feet smeared with mud.
Doubting him, he was questioned by the family members.
He gave evasive reply.
It was, therefore, suspected that the appellant after raping the victim, has killed her.
Later, the dead-body was recovered from a marshy place near the house of the informant.
5. The deceased appears to have been strangulated to death.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant has argued that it is at best a case of circumstantial evidence and the linkages between the offence and the appellant have not been established beyond all reasonable doubts.

7. However, looking at the accusation against Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.503 of 2023(4)
dt.07-10-2024 the appellant and the circumstances indicating that it was the appellant in whose company the deceased had been playing and later she was found dead, we are not inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant.
8. The prayer for suspension of sentence of the appellant is rejected.

(Ashutosh Kumar, J) (Jitendra Kumar, J) Sauravkrsinha/ Krishna- U T Pradeep Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95342182/
